cards.title: The Book, with live previews
cards.text: Every hero ability, enemy move, status and trinket plays live in the Book. Pick a hero and a tier. Live as 0.15.0.
cards.why: You asked for the Riffle clips inside the game, simulated, for every unit, ability and tier, and a Book overhaul. Mark what reads badly.
cards.details:
Known limits. Where a tier only changes a number (a percentage, a duration, a crit), the picture is the same at each tier and the tier's own words rise on the stage instead: that's 56 abilities. Bosses play in a small yard, not their own hall. A status is always shown on a goblin.

A check runs all 2,066 previews and fails if one breaks or its move never happens, so new heroes and enemies get previews without extra work.

parts.title: Layout
parts.text: The preview on top; under it what's playing and its numbers; then the moves, the tier dial and a strip of faces, all under your thumb. Tabs: Heroes, Monsters, Statuses, Items.

parts.title: Heroes and tiers
parts.text: All 52 heroes. The dial sets tier 0 to III; the attack, each ability and the trait play at that tier, with the numbers at that tier. An ability the tier hasn't unlocked shows locked.

parts.title: Traits
parts.text: Each trait is staged in the moment it matters, and its words rise off the hero when it acts ("blocked 35%").

parts.title: Monsters
parts.text: By dungeon; ones you haven't met stay hidden. Normal, elite and major, each with its moves against dummies, and the trinket an elite carries.

parts.title: Statuses and items
parts.text: Each status builds on a dummy until it bursts, with its rules in plain words. Each trinket and potion is shown doing its thing.

cards.title: The wagon, round two
cards.text: Four times the ground, a bigger wagon, pulled back, a real forest edge, a shop, no switch.
cards.why: Your list and your wagon answers, built. Mark what's still off; the forest is the part I most want your eye on.
cards.details:
In tests parties at level 3, 4 and 5 deliver the wagon 42%, 50% and 67% of the time.

With the ground this wide, the screen shows open meadow when nothing is happening and a tree line only comes into view when the fight is near it. Say if you'd rather see the trees all the time; that means zooming out further or narrowing the ground.

Still weak: small flower and grass marks on the meadow; the Burnt Wood's glowing cracks read as scribbles; the later countries are too hard for the level you'd reach them at.

parts.title: Ground, wagon, camera
parts.text: The open ground is about 4 times as wide, the wagon about twice as long with two oxen, and the camera pulled back. The camera leans to where the fight is.

parts.title: The forest edge
parts.text: Several kinds of tree, fallen trunks reaching onto the verge, bushes, faceted rocks. Every wave walks out from under the canopy; a red arrow at the screen's edge marks one coming from off screen.

parts.title: Gold, no switch
parts.text: The switch is gone. Heroes pick up gold near them, and go further when nothing threatens. The Quartermaster and the Pirate are gatherers: they go for gold first, even mid-fight.

parts.title: The downed
parts.text: A downed hero can be revived on the road until they scroll off behind the wagon; then they wait at the next camp.

parts.title: The roadside shop
parts.text: Spends only the gold picked up on this trip: mend the wagon, a healing draught, a trinket, a sellsword. What you don't spend, you keep.

parts.title: Other countries
parts.text: Each beaten dungeon opens its own country as a stretch: snow pines, the burnt wood, and so on.

parts.title: No more huddling
parts.text: With nothing to fight, heroes walk spread out instead of bunching, in dungeons too.
